content.text:
**OpenAI has significantly evolved its agent-related APIs and tools, with major updates in 2025–2026.** The core shift moved away from the older Assistants API and experimental Swarm toward the **Responses API** (as the flagship primitive for agentic workflows) and the **Agents SDK** (a production-ready framework for orchestrating single- and multi-agent systems).[[1]](https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/)

### Key Recent Updates (as of 2026)
- **April 2026: Next Evolution of the Agents SDK** — OpenAI released an updated Agents SDK that adds a more capable harness for agents working with documents, files, and systems. New features include:
  - Configurable memory
  - Sandbox-aware orchestration
  - Codex-like filesystem tools
  - Standardized integrations with primitives like MCP (for tool use), skills (progressive disclosure), AGENTS.md (custom instructions), shell tool (code execution), apply patch tool (file edits), and more
  - Better scalability: support for one or many sandboxes, isolated subagent environments, and parallelization across containers
  - Sandbox integration for safer, siloed operations (e.g., accessing files/code only for specific tasks while protecting overall system integrity)

  This is generally available to all customers via the API with standard token- and tool-use-based pricing. It launched first in Python, with TypeScript support following. Additional capabilities like code mode and subagents are in development for both languages.[[2]](https://openai.com/index/the-next-evolution-of-the-agents-sdk/)

- **Responses API as the Foundation** — Positioned as the new default for building agents. It combines the simplicity of Chat Completions with built-in tools and stateful/agentic capabilities. It supports a built-in agent execution loop, shell tools, hosted container workspaces, context compaction, reusable agent skills, and multi-agent features (beta in 2026 with GPT-5.6 models, allowing one root agent to spawn/coordinate parallel subagents). Developers are encouraged to start here rather than managing their own loops.[[3]](https://platform.openai.com/docs/llms-full.txt)

- **Deprecations and Migrations**:
  - **Assistants API**: Set to be deprecated (target sunset in mid-2026, with full parity in Responses API).
  - **Agent Builder** (visual canvas from AgentKit, launched 2025) and **Evals platform**: Deprecated in June 2026; full shutdown on November 30, 2026 (Evals becomes read-only earlier). Migrate to the code-first Agents SDK, Workspace Agents in ChatGPT, or alternatives like Promptfoo.
  - **Swarm** (2024 experimental): Fully superseded by the Agents SDK in 2025; the repo now redirects to it. The SDK adds guardrails, tracing, sessions, hosted tools, realtime voice, and sandbox agents while retaining core handoff primitives.[[4]](https://mcp.directory/blog/openai-agentkit-deprecation-2026)

- **Other Enhancements**:
  - Built-in tools (web search, file search, computer use, tool search, etc.) and support for protocols like MCP.
  - Multi-agent capabilities, realtime/voice agents, and enterprise features like Workspace Agents (successor to custom GPTs, with integrations into tools like Slack/Salesforce).
  - SDKs available in Python (`openai-agents-python`) and TypeScript/JavaScript (`openai-agents-js`), with ongoing releases (e.g., v0.11+ in early 2026 adding tool search and GA computer use).[[5]](https://newreleases.io/project/github/openai/openai-agents-python/release/v0.11.0)

### Official Resources
- OpenAI's announcement on the Agents SDK evolution: https://openai.com/index/the-next-evolution-of-the-agents-sdk/
- Documentation and SDK repos: GitHub (openai/openai-agents-python and openai/openai-agents-js), platform.openai.com/docs
- Migration guides for deprecated tools are available in the developer portal.

These changes reflect OpenAI's push toward safer, more scalable, production-ready agent building with less boilerplate for developers. For the absolute latest, check the official OpenAI blog or developers site, as the ecosystem continues to iterate rapidly.
